source: Phase 5: sections for the 7 forms. prf_programme shows the skip rule — people with no work experience skip the programme-experience section (TDD §7.2 example).

data.title: Your background
data.instructions: Start with your CV, then a few questions about your education and experience. There are no right or wrong answers.

data.title: Programme experience
data.instructions: Tell us about the change and project work you have done.

data.title: Your motivation
data.instructions: Help us understand what you want from a consulting career.

data.title: How you work
data.instructions: For each question, put the four statements in order — most like you at the top, least like you at the bottom. Drag them, or use the arrow buttons. There are no right answers.

data.title: What matters to you (1 of 2)
data.instructions: Each statement describes a person. How much is this person like you? Answer quickly — your first reaction is best.

data.title: What matters to you (2 of 2)
data.instructions: Each statement describes a person. How much is this person like you?

data.title: Executive memo
data.instructions: Write as you would to a senior client: clear, structured and brief — or record a short video and upload it instead. Your written answer saves automatically.

data.title: Case: Harbour Bank
data.instructions:
Harbour Bank is a regional retail bank with 1.2 million customers and 140 branches.

• Customers under 35 have fallen 18% in two years, mostly to app-only banks.
• Its mobile app is rated 2.9 out of 5; most complaints are about slow onboarding and card controls.
• Branches account for 55% of operating costs; branch visits are down 30% since 2021.
• Customers over 50 are loyal and hold 70% of deposits.

The CEO asks: “How do we win back younger customers while reducing our cost to serve — without losing our loyal older customers?”

Answer the two questions below — type your answer, or upload a document (PDF, Word or PowerPoint). Typed answers save automatically.
